newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US makes new offer in WTO financial services talks.
newsitem.headline: US makes new offer in WTO financial services talks.

text.p: The United States on Monday made a new offer in World Trade Organisation (WTO) talks aimed at reaching a global pact on liberalising financial services by the end of the year, diplomats said.
The move followed submission of new offers by Japan last Friday and by the European Union at the end of last month.

Canada, the fourth of the "Quad" group of top trading powers who recently jointly pledged to get updated proposals on the table by this week, was expected to follow suit later in the day or on Tuesday, according to the diplomats.
The packages from the four will provide a focus of interest during meetings between officials of many of the 131 members of the WTO in Geneva this week to assess progress in the talks.
All offers in the negotiations -- which have continued in different forms for nearly a decade under the WTO and its predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) -- are conditional.

U.S. officials say the talks, relaunched in April, can only succeed if key emerging economies match Washington proposals with similar packages giving foreign companies and service providers wide access to their markets.
The United States pulled out of an earlier effort to get a worldwide deal in 1995, saying developing countries were not going far enough.

An interim pact, which runs out in December, was then forged by the EU. But participants say they will not renew it if the latest drive for a pact embracing the United States, the world's biggest actor in the financial services sector, fails.
This would leave the booming global industry largely dependent on bilateral deals between individual countries for access to foreign markets.
